name: Lightning Rising Centre by Centre
previous_label: Adho Mukha Svanasana — Downward-Facing Dog (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: udgacchantīṃ taḍidrūpāṃ praticakraṃ kramāt kramam | ūrdhvaṃ muṣṭitrayaṃ yāvat tāvad ante mahodayaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
sanskrit_variants: GRETIL and Pradīpaka read taḍitrūpām; Wallis and Singh read taḍidrūpāṃ (same word, 'lightning-formed', different sandhi spelling). Wallis prints urddhvaṃ for ūrdhvaṃ.
dharana.rendering: Contemplate her rising like lightning, from centre to centre (cakra) in sequence, upward as far as three fists above the head; at the end there is the great dawning (mahodaya).
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh identifies the power as kuṇḍalinī and 'three fists' as the dvādaśānta. Singh contrasts it with verse 28: here the power climbs through the centres one by one, whereas in verse 28 it goes straight up.

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y3 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 29 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: successive centres (cakras) along the central line
three fists above the crown (Singh: dvādaśānta)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a vertical line with stations along it, and a quick flash of light passing station by station to a point about three fists above the head.
geometry.svg_hint: a vertical line with small marks for centres, a zig-zag flash moving up, ending at a point well above the head
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Flash and settle
reaction.summary: School metaphor: a brief flash of attention rises and then settles into open brightness. Not a biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: ordinary breath; a slightly longer out-breath helps the body stay settled
breath.cue: Ordinary breath, about four in and six out if counting helps. No forced hold. Never use the breath to drive the image.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient upward through the centres, then rest in the space above the head
orientation.gravity: Body settled and supported; the rising is only imagined
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Attention moving centre by centre up the central line to a point above the head
attention.secondary: Resting in the open space at the end
attention.chakra: cakras in sequence (named in the verse as praticakram, 'each centre')

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Contemplate her rising like lightning, from centre to centre (cakra) in sequence, upward as far as three fists above the head; at the end there is the great dawning (mahodaya).
adiyogi.method_summary: Gentle form: quietly mark attention centre by centre up the central line (base, belly, heart, throat, brow, crown), then rest awareness in the space above the crown for a breath or two. Contemplative tracing only; never try to produce rushes, heat or shaking, and never force sensation or breath.

honesty.disclosure: Door 006 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 6 (verse 29) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 006 is dharana 6, verse 29. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture] and VBT method are paired by School of 112 Doorways door number (D-006 with dharana 006). That link is a teaching device, not ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Both invite attention along a continuous central line. That shared metaphor supports the braid in class, but does not upgrade the pairing beyond school_device.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This school teaches only a slow, gentle tracing of this dharana. If it brings agitation, strong sensations or emotion, stop, open the eyes and ground attention in the feet. People who have had strong reactions to energy-focused meditation should choose a breath or sound door instead (for example Door 001 or Door 015). If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: [retired posture] ([retired posture]) or [retired posture] if wrists, shoulders, or hamstrings complain.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease off if wrists, shoulders, or low back complain; bend knees freely; do not force heels to the floor.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 006: lightning rising centre by centre. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 6, verse 29.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat, or lie down. The map is a vertical line with stations, ending about three fists above the head.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the body be supported and still. Eyes closed or lowered. Orient upward.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Ordinary breath, about four in, six out. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Quietly mark each centre in turn, base to crown, then rest in the space above the head.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a brief flash rises and settles into open brightness. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 29: the power rises like lightning, centre by centre, to three fists above the head, and at the end there is a great dawning. Trace gently. Never force.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the image go. Feel the feet and the floor. Open the eyes.
